mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate over the prior three months signals a tightening monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises by >0.25% q/q over last 3 months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly negative (< -1%) in at least 70% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% indicates weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the unemployment rate above 6.5% for two consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which depresses consumer spending and corporate margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly negative (< -1%) in at least 60% of triggered months.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 1% signals contraction in manufacturing activity, which reduces input demand and corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered months.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in both the federal funds rate and the Consumer Price Index above their respective 12-month averages signals a dual shock of monetary tightening and rising inflation, which erodes real corporate earnings and triggers negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly negative (< -1%) in at least 50% of triggered months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in housing starts (HOUST) below 1 million units for three consecutive months indicates a sharp contraction in the residential construction sector, which negatively impacts materials and financial firms, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A positive year-over-year change in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) exceeding 3% combined with an unemployment rate below 4% signals a tight labor market, which increases wage pressures and cost of capital, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days in an otherwise neutral macro environment.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly positive (> +1%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly increase in real personal savings (RSAFS) above its 12-month average, coupled with a decline in personal consumption expenditures growth (implied from GDPC1), signals a shift from spending to saving, which reduces near-term demand and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS > 12-mo avg AND implied consumption growth < 0%
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are not significantly negative (< -1%) in at least 50% of triggered episodes.
